summary: Discovery call to map Cerulean's integration needs for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer is evaluating SDK support (Python/JS), LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters, a gateway/proxy pattern for routing, strict rate limits and quota enforcement, and observability hooks to tie into their existing logging and tracing. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO, Cerulean), Jules Martin (Lead ML Eng), Rosa Kim (Platform Eng)

Summary: quick discovery on integration surface and pilot scope.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and Liam our solutions engineer is here too. Quick intro round?
[00:12] Samir Patel: Hi Samir here, CTO at Cerulean. We're building a customer insights platform with realtime ingest and LLM-based summarization pipelines.
[00:18] Jules Martin: Jules, lead ML engineer. We're evaluating how to stitch LLMs into our existing LangChain stacks.
[00:24] Rosa Kim: Rosa, platform. Responsible for infra, VPCs, security controls.
[00:28] Liam O'Connor: Liam, SE. I'll talk through integration patterns and observability.

[01:05] Maya Chen: Great. Goal for today is to understand your integration constraints — SDKs, gateways, quotas, and any private deployment requirements. Also timeline and success criteria.
[01:17] Samir Patel: Our main questions are: can we start on Hosted to prototype then move to Dedicated or Private for production? How intrusive are SDK changes? Also need clear SLAs around latency and a way to enforce per-tenant rate limits.
[01:35] Jules Martin: And specifically: we use LangChain and LlamaIndex in python. Do you have first-class adapters? Is there an example repo?

[02:00] Liam O'Connor: Short answer: yes. Redwood has official SDKs for Python and Node with a LangChain connector and community LlamaIndex adapters — we have example repos. For Hosted you can use the SDK directly; for Dedicated or Private you can point the SDK to your dedicated endpoint or private gateway. I'll share a LangChain example repo after the call.
[02:22] Rosa Kim: When you say private gateway, do you mean a proxy in our VPC that forwards to Redwood, or a fully customer-hosted inference runtime?
[02:32] Liam O'Connor: We support both patterns. For Private deployments we offer a customer-managed control plane with an on-prem serving option. For a lighter lift you can run a gateway/proxy in your VPC that routes requests to Hosted or Dedicated with TLS and mTLS. That gateway can also enforce per-tenant quotas.

[03:05] Samir Patel: Good — we'd prefer a gateway at first. But we need guaranteed data isolation for PII; is prefix caching or caching stored somewhere on Redwood side?
[03:18] Maya Chen: Caching can be configured; for Hosted we have optional prefix/KV caching which by default is ephemeral and tied to the request lifecycle. For Dedicated/Private you can enforce no cross-tenant caching. We'll document the defaults in the security whitepaper.

[04:00] Jules Martin: About rate limits: can we set strict per-API-key quotas and burst windows? We want hard throttles per customer so a noisy tenant doesn't affect others.
[04:12] Liam O'Connor: Yes. Redwood's rate limiting supports per API key and route-based quotas. For Dedicated you can configure more granular policies and custom throttles. There's also a token-level budgeting control we can hook into your CDN/gateway. Some customers run the quota enforcement in their gateway for absolute control.

[05:00] Rosa Kim: Observability is critical — we use Datadog and OpenTelemetry. Can Redwood emit traces and token-level latency metrics to our observability stack?
[05:12] Liam O'Connor: Redwood Console exposes dashboards and trace hooks. For Private/Dedicated we have a forwarder and OTEL exporter you can enable that sends spans to your OTLP endpoint. Hosted exposes webhooks and logs; we can provide log-forwarding via S3 or realtime webhooks for events.

[06:15] Samir Patel: Any limitations with the SDKs? For example long streaming responses and reconnects — we stream tokens in our UI.
[06:26] Liam O'Connor: SDK supports streaming and resumable streams. There are edge cases with long lived connections behind proxies; the recommendation is to use Redwood's SSE or websocket streaming. We'll provide a sample React + SDK streaming example.

[07:05] Jules Martin: On the model side: we need many short-context calls and some long generation tasks. Any guidance about batching and cost tuning?
[07:17] Maya Chen: Redwood Optimize gives batching and quantization suggestions per workload. For short bursts, small batch sizes keep tail latency low; for heavy throughput you can increase batch size and enable prefix caching. We'll run a small benchmark to recommend configs for your traffic profile.

[08:00] Rosa Kim: Security items — SOC 2, SSO/SAML for console, RBAC, and KMS integration for keys. Also audit logs retention.
[08:10] Maya Chen: We have SOC 2 and can share the cert and whitepaper. SSO/SAML with SCIM for provisioning and RBAC are available for Dedicated and Private. KMS integration supported for both Dedicated and Private — Hosted supports customer-managed keys via an HSM integration for higher tiers. Audit logs can be exported to your logging bucket for the retention window you specify.

[09:05] Samir Patel: Pricing — what's the runway to test on Hosted? We want to do a pilot for 2–4 weeks with some benchmarking.
[09:18] Maya Chen: We can provide trial credits and a pilot pricing template. For production we recommend Dedicated if you need consistent tail latency and per-tenant isolation; Dedicated pricing is commit-based monthly/annual. We'll send a couple of commit scenarios.

[10:05] Jules Martin: For the LangChain adapter: does it support callback handlers to integrate Redwood's traces into LangChain's callbacks?
[10:18] Liam O'Connor: Yes we expose callbacks and tracing hooks. The LangChain connector plugs into LC's callback system so you can capture token-level events and spans. Small caveat: some community adapters use slightly different callback signatures — we have patches in the example repo.

[11:00] Rosa Kim: Latency SLOs — what's realistic: p95 and p99 for 512 token completions?
[11:12] Liam O'Connor: For Dedicated on A100/4x setups customers commonly see p95 under 220ms and p99 under 400–500ms for typical models; numbers vary by model and sequence length. Hosted has published profiles; we'll attach the performance profiles.

[12:05] Samir Patel: Any concerns with data residency? We have EU clients and need EU-hosted endpoints.
[12:16] Maya Chen: We have regional hosting in EU and NA. For strict residency you'd want Dedicated or Private in the EU region; Hosted can be pinned to EU cluster as well for enterprise accounts.

[13:00] Jules Martin: Integration checklist for us: 1) LangChain/LlamaIndex example 2) benchmark script and sample dataset 3) Hosted trial keys 4) Security docs and SOC2 5) pricing/commit scenarios.
[13:18] Maya Chen: Yep that's what we'll deliver. Liam will share the sample repos and scripts.

[14:00] Rosa Kim: Operational question: how do you handle model rollouts and fallbacks? We want automatic fallback to a cheaper LLM when capacity is constrained.
[14:12] Liam O'Connor: Smart routing policies can route by latency/cost/region and automatic fallback is supported; you can set per-route fallback to a compatible model variant. We'll include our routing policy examples.

[15:00] Samir Patel: Ok good. Anything else?
[15:04] Maya Chen: Quick recap then next steps.

End recap and next steps:
- Redwood to send pricing deck and Dedicated commit examples (Maya)
- SE to share LangChain/LlamaIndex example repo and benchmark script (Liam)
- Cerulean to send traffic profile and retention needs (Rosa)
- Follow-up deep dive scheduled for week of 2027-09-06

Call ended around 15:42 UTC.

Notes on transcription: occasional ASR mislabels (LamaIndex vs LlamaIndex) and punctuation; names mostly correct.
